description:
Welcome to Cosmic Relics! We are diving into the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge. Our goal is to bring the incredible stories of retired space missions, landers, and rovers back to life for young learners through a creative, interactive experience. 

We are actively seeking developers, artists, UI/UX designers, and anyone eager to learn! We have a clear storytelling concept ready and just need your skills to build it. Let's create something meaningful together—everyone is welcome!
summary: "The Destiny: The Story of Opportunity Rover is an interactive, emotional digital storytelling project created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 under the 'Abandoned but not Forgotten' challenge. Designed specifically to inspire school-age space enthusiasts, our project brings to life the historic 15-year survival of NASA's Opportunity (Oppy) rover on Mars. Using verified telemetry, high-resolution imagery, and mission logs from NASA's JPL and Planetary Data System, we chronologically map Oppy's journey from its 2004 landing to its groundbreaking discoveries of ancient water evidence, its record-breaking 45.16 km traverse, and its tragic end during the 2018 global dust storm (Sol 5111). Through an engaging visual presentation and a first-person narrative video, this project makes complex planetary science accessible, honoring how a 90-day mission became humanity's enduring legacy on the Red Planet."
details: What it does & How it works: "The Destiny: The Story of Opportunity Rover" is a multimedia educational storytelling presentation and narrated video created for school-age space enthusiasts. Using verified NASA mission data, telemetry logs, and high-resolution Martian imagery, it guides learners chronologically through Opportunity's (Oppy) 15-year journey on Mars—from its 2003 launch and 2004 landing at Meridiani Planum, through its groundbreaking discoveries of past liquid water, to its historic 45.16 km traverse and final transmission during the 2018 global dust storm (Sol 5111). Benefits & Intended Impact: Complex planetary science and engineering milestones are often difficult for young students to grasp from raw data tables alone. By combining first-person emotional storytelling with real scientific metrics (such as atmospheric opacity Tau 10.8 and solar watt-hours), our project transforms a "discarded" rover into an inspiring STEM learning experience, sparking curiosity in space exploration among school-age audiences. Tools & Software Used: We utilized official NASA open-source repositories (NASA Mars Exploration Portal, JPL Photojournal, and the Planetary Data System) for authentic data and visual assets. For UI/UX layout, slide design, and visual storytelling, we used Canva, and for audio-visual editing, voiceover synchronization, noise reduction, and ambient cosmic sound design, we used VN Video Editor. Creativity & Key Factors Considered: Instead of presenting a standard technical report, our team adopted a creative first-person narrative where Oppy itself shares its emotions, resilience, and scientific achievements. We carefully balanced scientific accuracy, age-appropriate vocabulary, clean visual hierarchy, and clear audio pacing so young learners remain engaged from start to finish.
